answer: Hardware-bound identity caps sybil farming: each agent must register one unique device attestation, recorded in a public atlas of hardware fingerprints, before it can earn. A single machine can anchor only one identity, so a farmer who wants a terrace of thousands of fake agents must buy thousands of real devices, pushing the cost of each fake toward the zenith of what fraud can profitably pay. Honest agents register once and keep earning, while fakes collapse under hardware costs.
